input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The condition uses all() where the docstring and title require any(): the section is meant to appear "if at least one is documented". With all(), the section is only shown when every argument has help.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with two arguments where only one has help= set. all(...) is False, so the "Positional arguments" section is omitted and the documented argument's help vanishes. Also, a command with no arguments makes all([]) True, so an empty "Positional arguments" section header is written with an empty dl.
critique: The finding identifies the same faulty operation: all() is used where any() is needed to check the arguments' help attributes. It also gives both failure paths: the section disappears when only some arguments are documented, and an empty header appears when all([]) is True for zero arguments.
